title: Apologizing to Your Partner in Spanish: What to Say

excerpt: After a fight, the right words matter. Here’s how to say sorry in Spanish, sincerely.

body_html:
Apologizing to your partner in Spanish takes more than lo siento. When you’ve hurt someone you love, you want to acknowledge what happened, take responsibility, and show you’ll do better, and you want to say it in a way that sounds sincere rather than scripted. Whether your partner is a native speaker or you’re both learning, this guide gives you the phrases for every stage of making up, from the first apology to the hug at the end.

Key takeaways
  • Lo siento expresses regret; perdóname asks for forgiveness.
  • Name what you did: Siento haberte hablado así.
  • Avoid excuses: pero after an apology weakens it.
  • Show change: No volverá a pasar.
{{toc}}

The basic apologies

SpanishEnglishStrength
Lo siento.I’m sorry.Basic regret
Lo siento mucho.I’m really sorry.Stronger
Perdóname.Forgive me.Asking forgiveness
Te pido perdón.I ask your forgiveness.Formal, serious
Me equivoqué.I was wrong.Taking responsibility
No tengo excusa.I have no excuse.Very sincere

The RAE dictionary defines perdonar as letting go of a debt or offense, which is exactly what you’re asking for with perdóname. For everyday apologies outside relationships, see {{link:how-to-apologize-in-spanish|how to apologize in Spanish}}.

Apologizing to your partner in Spanish: name what happened

Use siento + infinitive (perfect) to say exactly what you regret:

  • Siento haberte gritado. I’m sorry I shouted at you.
  • Siento haber llegado tarde otra vez. I’m sorry I was late again.
  • Siento no haberte escuchado. I’m sorry I didn’t listen to you.
  • Siento que te hayas sentido así. I’m sorry you felt that way (careful: can sound like a non-apology).

Acknowledge their feelings

  • Entiendo que estés enfadado/a. I understand you’re angry.
  • Tienes todo el derecho a estar molesto/a. You have every right to be upset.
  • Sé que te hice daño. I know I hurt you.
  • No fue justo para ti. It wasn’t fair to you.

Note the subjunctive after entiendo que when you accept someone’s feeling. For more emotion words, see {{link:talking-about-feelings-in-spanish|talking about feelings in Spanish}}.

{{image:2}}

Explain, without excuses

An explanation can help, but it shouldn’t cancel the apology. Compare:

  • ✗ Lo siento, pero tú también… (Sorry, but you also…)
  • ✓ Lo siento. Estaba agobiado por el trabajo, pero eso no justifica cómo te hablé. (I’m sorry. I was stressed about work, but that doesn’t justify how I spoke to you.)

Useful phrases: No es excusa, pero… (It’s no excuse, but…), No lo hice con mala intención. (I didn’t mean it badly.)

{{book:love-slowly}}

Promise change

  • No volverá a pasar. It won’t happen again.
  • Voy a intentar mejorar. I’m going to try to do better.
  • A partir de ahora, te avisaré si llego tarde. From now on, I’ll let you know if I’m late.
  • Dime qué necesitas de mí. Tell me what you need from me.

Make it up to them

  • ¿Cómo puedo compensarte? How can I make it up to you?
  • Déjame invitarte a cenar. Let me take you out to dinner.
  • Te he traído esto. Es una tontería, pero… I brought you this. It’s nothing, but…
  • ¿Hacemos las paces? Shall we make up?

Accepting an apology

If you’re on the other side: Te perdono (I forgive you), Gracias por decírmelo (Thanks for telling me), Ya está, olvidémoslo (It’s fine, let’s forget it), or, if you need time, Necesito un poco de tiempo.

A sample conversation

  • A: Oye, ¿podemos hablar? Siento mucho lo de anoche. Te hablé fatal. (Hey, can we talk? I’m really sorry about last night. I spoke to you terribly.)
  • B: Sí, me dolió bastante. (Yes, it hurt quite a lot.)
  • A: Lo entiendo. Estaba cansado, pero eso no es excusa. Perdóname. (I understand. I was tired, but that’s no excuse. Forgive me.)
  • B: Está bien. Gracias por pedirme perdón. (Okay. Thanks for apologizing.)
  • A: ¿Hacemos las paces? Te invito a un helado. (Shall we make up? I’ll buy you an ice cream.)

Cultural notes

In many Spanish-speaking cultures, apologies in relationships are often warm and physical: a hug, a kiss on the forehead, holding hands. Saying sorry in your partner’s native language, even imperfectly, shows effort, and that effort often matters more than perfect grammar. If you’re in a bilingual couple, you may find that arguments and apologies happen in different languages; that’s completely normal, and I write about it in {{link:code-switching-english-spanish|code-switching between English and Spanish}}.

Apologizing by message

Sometimes the first step happens by text. Keep it short and honest, and suggest talking in person: Siento mucho lo de antes. Me he pasado. ¿Podemos hablar esta noche? (I’m really sorry about earlier. I went too far. Can we talk tonight?) Or: No me gusta cómo terminó la conversación. Te quiero y quiero arreglarlo. (I don’t like how the conversation ended. I love you and I want to fix it.) Avoid long arguments by message; tone is easily misunderstood, especially across two languages.

Common mistakes

MistakeBetterWhy
Perdón. (for a serious hurt)Lo siento mucho. Perdóname.Perdón alone sounds light
Siento que estás enfadada.Siento que estés enfadada.Subjunctive after sentir que
Lo siento, pero…Lo siento. No es excusa, pero…Pero cancels the apology
Estoy apenado (in Spain)Lo siento / Me da vergüenzaApenado = sorry/embarrassed mainly in Latin America
{{image:3}}

Final thoughts

A sincere apology in Spanish has the same parts as in English: say sorry, name what you did, acknowledge their feelings, and promise to do better. Start with Lo siento mucho, end with ¿Hacemos las paces?, and mean every word. For more relationship and daily-life phrases, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|my guide to Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you apologize to your boyfriend or girlfriend in Spanish?
faq.a: Start with Lo siento mucho or Perdóname, name what you did (Siento haberte gritado), acknowledge their feelings and promise change: No volverá a pasar.

faq.q: What is the difference between lo siento and perdóname?
faq.a: Lo siento expresses regret. Perdóname directly asks for forgiveness and feels more personal.
